sections.notes: PM 18h is fireplace/shingle/selection coordination and scheduling (procurement); TL 8h + GL 4h staging/protection. JBD carries $0 permits but Tri-Cities pulls the permit per answer, so permit_items inherits the coordination hours.

Excavate, gravel, forms, reinforcement, slab pour with turned-down post footings and fireplace footing — this slab is the foundation/floor and precedes framing, so it belongs to groundwork, not concrete_landscape.
Posts, built-up beam, rafters, tie-in, sheathing, chimney-penetration framing.

Knee-wall framing + site-built screen frames → structural_framing; lap siding on knee wall → cladding_roof; beadboard, trim, screening, screen door → interior_installs. JBD priced 2' vinyl + spline system; answered spec is 3'-4" lap/beadboard + stapled wood frames.
Framed chase + firebox + Class A pipe set by in-house crew → structural_framing; chimney roof flashing/storm collar/cap → cladding_roof.
Interior stone veneer, hearth, mantel → interior_installs; exterior brick veneer on the chase (drawing p.5) → cladding_roof, though JBD does not separately price the exterior brick.

sections.section_name: Electrical (As Specifically Listed - NONE Listed - Flag)
sections.notes: Zero-electrical scope per answer; the 6h is coordination/acknowledgement only and pays for no rough_meps work.

flags.message: JBD screened enclosure carries ~60 LF of 2' vinyl knee wall with a spline screen system, but the plan shows only two open sides (~36 LF, ~33 LF after the door) and the answered spec is a 3'-4" lap-sided/beadboard knee wall with site-built stapled wood screen frames — the LF is overstated while the per-foot effort is understated, so 48h should not be trusted as a per-LF rate.

Footprint: proposal ~12.5' x 23.5' (294 sqft) vs drawings 22'-11" x 11'-8" clear (~267 sqft) / 24' x 12' overall — proposal governs per canon and the 9% spread is small, but field measurement will set the real slab and roof quantities.

JBD carries $0 permits and no inspection hours, while the answer has Tri-Cities pulling the building permit with four AHJ inspections (footing, framing, fireplace/chimney, final) — four inspection holds and their coordination are absent from the 390h and from the ~5-6 wk duration.

JBD prices 5 posts 'to approved bearing' with no post footings; the answered design uses turned-down footings in the slab AND a beam on posts alongside the house, which adds footing forming/rebar to concrete_patio and likely 2-3 posts to roof framing beyond the JBD count.

Fireplace structure at 98h (90h GL) plus 40h finish = 138h, 35% of all labor, for a 6'-wide framed chase with a manufactured firebox and Class A pipe built by the in-house crew — plausible only if the exterior brick veneer on the chase (drawing p.5, not priced in the JBD) is absorbed here; treat as an upper bound, not a per-sqft rate.
JBD carries 6h/$329 of electrical for a scope that is answered zero-electrical; those hours are coordination only and should not become a rough_meps task.
Proposal cover title and sole line item say 'Deck' but no deck exists anywhere in the scope, JBD, or drawings — the deck component receives nothing.

No roof pitch, rafter spacing, or post spacing is stated in any source; roof area (~330 sqft) and rafter count (19) are derived from the JBD's 3.3 sq / 19 rafters and geometry, so roofing and framing quantities are medium confidence until the eave tie-in height is field-measured.

The patio slab is mapped to groundwork rather than concrete_landscape because it is the porch floor and foundation (turned-down post footings, fireplace footing) and must precede framing; downstream should not schedule any late-phase concrete.

Drawings show white fascia/soffit and a screened transom band on the high side; the answer excludes fascia/soffit/gutters (bare framing), but the transom screen area is in neither the proposal narrative nor the JBD's screen lot — small added screen framing not priced.
